 Sun to screen: Junior develops an app for skin protection
 Ava Au , Social Media Manager 
 November 3, 2026 
 Junior Aditya Zanzaria developed an app called “SkinWise,” focusing on skin health and protection. He said he plans to pursue a career in the medical field as a dermatologist. Ava Au 
 “Don’t forget to put on sunscreen,” his dad nags at him as he leaves for tennis practice.  
 Under the blazing sun, he wonders how much sunscreen and what kind he should use. Because the skin is the biggest part of the body, his family has always been big on protecting their skin, but he never had an answer to his question. 
 Junior Aditya Zanzaria created “SkinWise,” an app made to scan skin and provide tips on how to prevent skin cancer and other concerns. Since middle school, Zanzaria was interested in and became familiar with coding softwares such as Python, Java and other programs. 
 “I was creating something I wanted other people to use,” Zanzaria said. “I want people to benefit from this, and it felt that I was helping out people because that’s the main thing [I wanted to do] with this app.” 
 He said at first, science wasn’t his strong suit, but after taking AP Biology during his freshman year, the challenging material and in-depth exploration of the subject helped him find his passion for science. 
 “When I took AP Biology, it was really a catalyst that helped spark my interest,” Zanzaria said. “I got to do labs in that class and learn the different biological functions. It really was interesting.” 
 Starting this January, Zanzaria continuously worked throughout the school year and into the summer to complete his app. He asked his dad Manish Zanzaria, who is a software engineer and has programmed apps in the past, to provide him feedback and tips on how to improve his coding.  
 “[Zanzaria] was spending hours and hours every day trying to get it done,” Manish Zanzaria said. “[He would try to] make it better and to test it out as much as possible. He spent a lot of time over the summer, even cancelling plans to focus on working on it.” 
 One of his biggest challenges was trying to program the app on Apple devices. Zanzaria originally developed the app for Android users, so he struggled with the unfamiliar code.  
 Exploring different softwares helped him identify these unrecognizable codes and fix them. During this period, he spent his time at his friend senior Shaan Reddy’s house to work on the IOS version of the app. 
 “He’s very resilient,” Reddy said. “There were times when I would have gotten frustrated, [but] he just went back and kept working. We went over [the program] over and over again with no breaks for hours.” 
 The app launched to Google Play and the App Store Sept. 19. Zanzaria said he hopes that his app reaches many people, especially student athletes in North Texas, since being in the tennis court was where his idea started. 
 “I had this mark on my hand that developed over the last [few] days,” Reddy said. “I used [Zanzaria’s] app to scan it, and it’s pretty impressive. I look at it frequently, mostly before tennis practice. All things considered, it’s a very useful app.” 
 Since its release, there have been fifty to a hundred downloads of the app. Some feedback he received was to create a Google or Apple sign-in. He took time to fix this issue, but found it surprising how many people rely on this feature. 
 “[Zanzaria looks for] solutions for the betterment of people and how to help people,” Manish Zanzaria said. “That is something which I’ve always seen about him: he cares and helps for different people.” 
 Zanzaria said he plans to pursue a career in the medical field as a dermatologist. He hopes that this project will allow him to explore various medical topics and spread awareness about skin health and protection. 
 “I wanted to create [an] impact with [the app],” Zanzaria said. “I was finally relieved because I was working on [it] for a while. [It] felt nice to finally have it on the App Store, something public, that everyone can use.”
